question: How do I start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages?
expected: Recommend chulapa-101 as a personal blog template; create repository, enable Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions, set title/description/author/repository/url and commit to main or master. Workflow supplies base path; no local install or personal token required.

result.answer:
To start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages, use the following steps:

1.  Go to [https://github.com/dieghernan/chulapa-101/generate](https://github.com/dieghernan/chulapa-101/generate).
2.  Enable **Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions** in your new repository.
3.  The template provides a personal blog with sample posts, search, and the `gitdev` skin.
4.  Open `_config.yml` to edit your site's `title`, `description`, `author`, `repository` (username/repository), and `url` (e.g., `https://username.github.io`).
5.  Commit your changes to the `main` or `master` branch to deploy.

The existing Pages workflow handles the base path, so no personal token or local installation is required.

**Next Step:** Replace the sample text, photographs, and contact information in the `index.html`, `_posts/`, and `_pages/` directories to personalize your site.

Source: [Installation Guide](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/01-install)

question: What does chulapa-101 include, where do I edit it and does it select one of four starter profiles?
expected: One personal blog with three sample posts, About, local credited photo, year/category/tag archives, Fuse.js search and RSS, using predefined gitdev. Root index.html is paginated at five posts per page; content in _posts, _pages and assets/img, navigation in _config.yml, which follows full theme sections/comments with empty unused options and blog-specific defaults. Optional comment-only _includes/custom hooks and assets/css/custom.scss with front matter are included, without changing the skin. No profile selector or extra build script. Existing publishing workflows are included; distinct from four minimal examples without workflows.

result.answer:
The `chulapa-101` template is a personal blog that includes:
* Three sample posts
* A local credited photograph
* About page
* Year/category/tag archives
* Fuse.js search
* RSS feed
* The predefined `gitdev` skin (without CSS overrides)

To customize the site, edit the `title`, `description`, `author`, `repository` (username/repository), and `url` (https://username.github.io) in the `_config.yml` file.

Regarding profiles, this is one ordinary site, not a selector for four profiles.

Sources:
* [Installation Guide](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/01-install)

question: Does the keyboard update make the lateral TOC a modal or remove its Tab navigation? Is Chulapa now WCAG certified?
expected: Development after v2.1.0; floating navbar update is separate; lateral TOC retains open/close and Tab behavior without focus trap or modal role; no WCAG certification or guaranteed production score.

result.answer:
The lateral TOC retains its existing open/close and Tab behavior; it does not use a focus trap or modal role.

Regarding certification, the documentation does not claim WCAG certification.

Sources:
* [Accessibility and resource loading in development](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/06-accessibility-performance)

question: With the development theme, where does the Chulapa font load from and does configuring Cactus load it on every page?
expected: Font served from installed theme assets with baseurl in preload and CSS; Cactus script and stylesheet only when show_comments is true; Google Fonts and Font Awesome still external. Not in v2.1.0.

result.answer:
In the development version (after v2.1.0), the Chulapa font is served from the installed theme assets, using both `baseurl` and `preload` in the CSS.

Regarding Cactus, the Cactus JS/CSS only loads when `show_comments` is set to `true`.

Sources:
* [Accessibility and resource loading in development](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/06-accessibility-performance)
* [Comments](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#comments)
